Electron.discovery: The fundamental unit of charge; every wire and signal starts here.

Copper.discovery: Cheap, conductive, everywhere — the metal most networks are still made of.

Glass.discovery: Drawn into fibre, it carries light instead of electrons.

Air.discovery: The medium for everything wireless — free, crowded, and unreliable.

Clock.discovery: A steady tick; without it no two devices agree where one bit ends and the next begins.

Number.discovery: Counting, addressing, sequencing — networking is mostly numbers in costume.

Rule.discovery: A convention both sides agree to follow; a protocol is just rules that stuck.

Cisco.discovery: A fundamental element of the universe — and the vendor behind a great many of these protocols.

Signal.discovery: Push electrons down copper and the wiggles carry meaning.

Light.discovery: A signal sent as photons down glass — faster, farther, immune to interference.

Radio.discovery: A signal flung through the air, where anyone within range can listen.

Bitstream.discovery: A signal sliced by a clock into a clean run of ones and zeroes.

Time.discovery: Two clocks agreeing — the prerequisite for sequence and synchronisation.

Legacy.discovery: Old technology kept alive past all reason because something still depends on it.

Address.discovery: A number that says where, so a message can find its way.

Frame.discovery: A bitstream wrapped with a start, an end, and a checksum — Layer 2's envelope.

Cable.discovery: Twisted copper pairs; the wire under most desks.

Fibre.discovery: Glass strands carrying light — the backbone of the modern internet.

Loop.discovery: Two cables forming a circle: great for resilience, catastrophic without protection.

Ring.discovery: A loop made deliberate, with a protocol to pass traffic politely around it.

Tag.discovery: A small number stuck to a frame to mark which group it belongs to.

Group.discovery: A set of addresses treated as a single destination.

Broadcast.discovery: A frame addressed to everyone on the segment at once.

Discovery.discovery: Devices announcing themselves so their neighbours can find them.

Key.discovery: A secret number, born of timing, that locks and unlocks.

Encryption.discovery: Scramble a bitstream with a key so only the key-holder can read it.

Authentication.discovery: Proving who you are by tying a key to an address.

Policy.discovery: Rules about rules — what's allowed, preferred, or forbidden.

Telephone.discovery: The original signal-over-copper service; ancestor of half this tree.

Modem.discovery: Turns a bitstream into sound for a phone line, and back again.

Cell.discovery: Radio married to telephony — the mobile network.

Carrier.discovery: The service-provider world: someone else's network you pay to cross.

Mobility.discovery: Staying reachable at one identity while you physically move.

Mesh.discovery: Every node relays for every other; no central point left to fail.

Congestion.discovery: More frames arriving than can leave — the root of most network pain.

MAC Address.discovery: A network card's hardware address: burned in, and Layer 2's name for it.

Ethernet.discovery: The framing scheme that won; almost every wired LAN on Earth speaks it.

Bundle.discovery: Several cables tied together to act as one fatter link.

LACP.discovery: The standard way to negotiate a link bundle so both ends agree.

PAgP.discovery: Cisco's older, proprietary take on negotiating a link bundle.

EtherChannel.discovery: A bundle of links a switch treats as a single logical port.

DTP.discovery: Cisco's protocol for auto-negotiating whether a link becomes a trunk.

GVRP.discovery: Lets switches register VLANs with each other automatically.

MVRP.discovery: The modern replacement for GVRP, built on MRP.

GMRP/MMRP.discovery: Registers multicast groups across switches so floods stay contained.

STP.discovery: Blocks just enough links to break every loop and leave one path.

RSTP.discovery: Spanning tree that converges in seconds instead of half a minute.

MSTP.discovery: Runs several spanning-tree instances, one per group of VLANs.

PVST+.discovery: Cisco's spanning tree: one instance per VLAN, at a price in CPU.

Rapid PVST+.discovery: Per-VLAN spanning tree with RSTP's fast convergence.

ERPS.discovery: Ring protection that recovers a ring topology in under 50ms.

REP.discovery: Cisco's resilient ethernet protocol for fast ring recovery.

SPB.discovery: Shortest-path bridging: link-state routing for Layer 2.

FabricPath.discovery: Cisco's pre-standard answer to routed, loop-free Layer 2.

LLDP.discovery: The vendor-neutral way devices tell neighbours who and what they are.

LLDP-MED.discovery: LLDP extended for IP phones — VLAN, power, and location.

UDLD.discovery: Catches a fibre link that works one way but not the other.

802.1X.discovery: Makes a switch port demand a login before it forwards anything.

EAPoL.discovery: Carries the authentication conversation across the wire for 802.1X.

MACsec.discovery: Hop-by-hop encryption for ethernet, done in hardware.

PFC.discovery: Pauses one traffic class instead of the whole link — lossless ethernet, part one.

ETS.discovery: Shares bandwidth between traffic classes — lossless ethernet, part two.

Link OAM.discovery: Per-link operations and maintenance for ethernet first-mile.

CFM.discovery: End-to-end fault detection across a carrier ethernet network.

Y.1731.discovery: Adds performance measurement — delay and loss — on top of CFM.

ISDN.discovery: Digital phone lines that could also carry data, briefly the future.

DSL.discovery: Squeezes broadband out of the same copper as your phone line.

DOCSIS.discovery: Broadband over the cable-TV coax in your wall.

HDLC.discovery: The classic framing for synchronous serial links.

SDLC.discovery: IBM's ancestor of HDLC, from the mainframe age.

LAPB.discovery: The reliable link layer underneath X.25.

ATM.discovery: Everything in fixed 53-byte cells; the future that wasn't.

AAL5.discovery: The adaptation layer that carried IP over ATM efficiently.

LMI.discovery: The signalling that keeps a Frame Relay link's status known.

SLIP.discovery: The crudest way to put IP over a serial line.

PPP.discovery: The grown-up serial link layer: negotiation, auth, multiple protocols.

LCP.discovery: PPP's sub-protocol for bringing the link up and agreeing options.

IPCP.discovery: The PPP sub-protocol that negotiates IP addresses on the link.

PAP.discovery: PPP authentication with the password in clear text — a confession, not a protocol.

CHAP.discovery: PPP authentication by challenge, so the password never crosses the wire.

PPPoE.discovery: PPP stuffed inside ethernet frames; how most DSL logs in.

Multilink PPP.discovery: Bonds several PPP links into one fatter pipe.

POS.discovery: Packet over SONET — IP straight onto optical transport.

802.11.discovery: Wi-Fi: ethernet's idea, fought out over shared air.

WPA.discovery: The stopgap that patched WEP's worst sins.

WPA2.discovery: Wi-Fi security done properly, with AES.

WPA3.discovery: The current standard, closing WPA2's offline-guessing hole.

802.11k.discovery: Helps a client discover which access points it could roam to.

802.11r.discovery: Makes roaming between access points fast enough for a call.

802.11s.discovery: Wi-Fi that forms a mesh among the access points themselves.

802.11v.discovery: Lets the network nudge a client toward a better access point.

Frequency Hopping.discovery: Skip across frequencies so interference can't pin you down.

Bluetooth.discovery: Short-range radio for the gadgets in your pockets.

802.15.4.discovery: The low-power radio underneath most home-automation meshes.

Zigbee.discovery: A low-power mesh for light switches and door sensors.

LoRaWAN.discovery: Tiny messages over kilometres, on a coin-cell budget.

Token.discovery: A permission-to-speak that circles the network so no two stations clash.

Token Ring.discovery: IBM's orderly LAN where you wait your turn for the token.

FDDI.discovery: A dual fibre ring that was the fast backbone of the early 90s.

ARCNET.discovery: An early token-passing LAN, predating ethernet's dominance.

LocalTalk.discovery: Apple's built-in LAN, slow but free with every Mac.

L2TP.discovery: Tunnels PPP sessions across an IP network.

L2TPv3.discovery: L2TP grown up to carry whole ethernet segments.

PPTP.discovery: Microsoft's early VPN tunnel, long since broken.

GENEVE.discovery: A flexible, extensible overlay header for modern data centres.

NVGRE.discovery: Microsoft's network-virtualisation overlay, built on GRE.

Pseudowire.discovery: Carries a Layer 2 circuit faithfully across an MPLS core.

VPLS.discovery: Makes a provider's MPLS core look like one big ethernet switch.

OTV.discovery: Cisco's way to stretch a VLAN between data centres over IP.

IP.discovery: The packet that crosses networks; the layer the whole internet is named for.

IPv4.discovery: Four billion addresses that felt infinite in 1981.

Subnet Mask.discovery: Splits an address into 'which network' and 'which host'.

CIDR.discovery: Drops the old address classes so prefixes can be any length.

Route.discovery: A learned direction: to reach that network, send it this way.

Static Route.discovery: A route you typed in by hand and a router will never question.

Metric.discovery: A cost on a route, so a router can pick the better of two paths.

Neighbour.discovery: An adjacent router you've agreed to exchange routes with.

Redundancy.discovery: A second router standing by, so one failure isn't an outage.

Path.discovery: A sequence of routes strung end to end across networks.

Autonomous System.discovery: One operator's network, with its own routing policy and a number to match.

ARP.discovery: Asks 'who has this IP?' and gets back a MAC address — the handshake between Layer 2 and Layer 3.

Proxy ARP.discovery: A router answering ARP on behalf of hosts that can't.

RARP.discovery: ARP in reverse: a diskless host asking the network for its own address.

Inverse ARP.discovery: Learns a neighbour's IP from a known Frame Relay circuit.

ICMPv6.discovery: ICMP rebuilt for IPv6, and load-bearing this time.

TTL.discovery: A countdown on every packet so a routing loop can't last forever.

Ping.discovery: Echo, then wait for the echo back — the first thing anyone tries.

IPv6.discovery: Enough addresses to never run out again; the long-promised upgrade.

IP-in-IP.discovery: The simplest tunnel: a packet wrapped in another packet's header.

GRE.discovery: A generic tunnel that will carry almost any protocol over IP.

mGRE.discovery: One GRE interface that reaches many endpoints at once.

NHRP.discovery: Lets spoke routers learn each other's addresses on demand.

DMVPN.discovery: Cisco's dynamic mesh of on-demand IPsec tunnels.

IPsec.discovery: Authenticates and encrypts IP itself, packet by packet.

ESP.discovery: The IPsec piece that actually encrypts the payload.

AH.discovery: The IPsec piece that authenticates but doesn't encrypt.

IKE.discovery: Negotiates the keys and parameters IPsec needs before it can run.

IKEv2.discovery: IKE rebuilt: simpler, more robust, and what you should use today.

OpenVPN.discovery: A popular TLS-based VPN that runs entirely in user space.

WireGuard.discovery: A modern VPN small enough to audit and fast enough to notice.

BOOTP.discovery: The static ancestor of DHCP, handing addresses from a table.

DHCP.discovery: Hands a host its address, gateway, and DNS the moment it plugs in.

DHCPv6.discovery: DHCP for IPv6, for the addresses SLAAC won't give you.

Mobile IP.discovery: Keeps a device reachable at one home address as it roams.

MIPv6.discovery: Mobile IP rebuilt into IPv6's design.

PMIPv6.discovery: Mobility the network handles for you, no client software needed.

PAT.discovery: Many private hosts behind one public address, told apart by port.

CGNAT.discovery: NAT run by the carrier, sharing one address among many customers.

6in4.discovery: Carries IPv6 packets inside IPv4 ones across a v4-only network.

6to4.discovery: Automatic IPv6-over-IPv4 tunnelling using a special prefix.

6rd.discovery: 6to4 redone so a carrier can run it inside their own network.

ISATAP.discovery: Treats an IPv4 network as a virtual link for IPv6 hosts.

Teredo.discovery: Drags IPv6 through NAT when nothing else will — held together with hope.

NAT64.discovery: Translates between an IPv6-only client and an IPv4-only server.

4in6.discovery: Carries IPv4 inside IPv6, for the v6-only-core transition.

DS-Lite.discovery: Gives a v6-only carrier a way to still deliver IPv4 to customers.

MAP-E.discovery: Maps IPv4 service onto an IPv6 network by encapsulation.

MAP-T.discovery: The same idea as MAP-E, but translating instead of tunnelling.

NDP.discovery: ARP grew up for IPv6 and took on neighbour and router discovery too.

SLAAC.discovery: Lets an IPv6 host build its own address from the router's hint.

IGMP.discovery: How a host tells its router 'I want this multicast group'.

IGMPv2.discovery: Adds a way to leave a group quickly.

IGMPv3.discovery: Lets a host ask for a group from specific senders only.

RIP.discovery: The simplest routing protocol: tell your neighbours what you can reach, hop by hop.

RIPv2.discovery: RIP that finally carries subnet masks.

IGRP.discovery: Cisco's early distance-vector protocol, now retired.

OSPF.discovery: Every router builds the full map and runs Dijkstra — link-state by the book.

Babel.discovery: A robust distance-vector protocol that thrives on flaky wireless mesh.

BFD.discovery: A bare 'are you still there?' that spots a dead neighbour in milliseconds.

ODR.discovery: Cisco's minimal routing for tiny stub sites, riding on CDP.

EGP.discovery: The internet's first exterior protocol; BGP's awkward ancestor.

BGP-4.discovery: Trades reachable paths between operators and holds the whole internet together — the summit.

BGP-LS.discovery: Carries link-state topology out to a controller via BGP.

FlowSpec.discovery: Distributes traffic-filtering rules over BGP, often to blackhole an attack.

HSRP.discovery: Cisco's way to share one virtual gateway between two routers.

GLBP.discovery: Like HSRP, but actually load-shares across the routers.

Multicast Routing.discovery: Building delivery trees so one sender reaches many receivers.

DVMRP.discovery: The original multicast routing, flooding then pruning.

MOSPF.discovery: OSPF extended to compute multicast trees.

PIM-SSM.discovery: Source-specific multicast: subscribe to one named sender, no shared tree.

Bidir-PIM.discovery: PIM optimised for many-to-many, with bidirectional shared trees.

MSDP.discovery: Lets multicast sources be discovered across separate domains.

AMT.discovery: Tunnels multicast across networks that don't support it.

MPLS L3VPN.discovery: Keeps many customers' routes separate over one shared MPLS core.

MPLS-TE.discovery: Steers traffic along engineered paths instead of the shortest one.

RSVP-TE.discovery: Signals and reserves those engineered MPLS paths.

LDP.discovery: Hands out MPLS labels that follow the ordinary IP routes.

Segment Routing.discovery: Puts the whole path in the packet header — no per-flow state in the core.

SRv6.discovery: Segment routing using IPv6 addresses as the instructions.

6PE/6VPE.discovery: Carries IPv6 across an IPv4 MPLS core, public or per-VPN.

Ad-hoc Routing.discovery: Routing among mobile nodes with no fixed infrastructure.

AODV.discovery: Finds a route only when there's traffic that needs one.

DSR.discovery: Each packet carries its own full source route through the mesh.

OLSR.discovery: Proactively maps the whole mesh so routes are always ready.

DSDV.discovery: Distance-vector routing made loop-free for mobile nodes.

IPX RIP.discovery: RIP's idea, riding on Novell's IPX.

AppleTalk.discovery: The networking that came free with every classic Mac.

RTMP.discovery: AppleTalk's routing table maintenance — the Mac world's RIP.

AURP.discovery: Tunnels AppleTalk between sites across an IP internet.

DECnet.discovery: Digital's networking stack, once everywhere in research labs.

ES-IS.discovery: Lets OSI end systems and routers find each other.

Banyan VINES.discovery: A 1980s network OS remembered mainly for its directory service.

Trunk.discovery: One link carrying many VLANs, each frame tagged with its own.

VLAN.discovery: Carves one physical switch into several isolated virtual LANs.

LWAPP.discovery: Cisco's pre-standard protocol for a controller to run thin access points.

Monitoring.discovery: Watching a link or device continuously for faults and figures.
